finding.claim: Streamable HTTP server never validates the Origin or Host header, so a DNS-rebinding web page can reach an unauthenticated localhost MCP server and invoke tools/call. Spec-required control missing; conditional on the app binding locally without its own auth.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled web page after DNS rebinding; POST headers (Origin/Host) are never read (grep for Origin|HTTP_HOST in lib/ returns nothing).
finding.sink: tools/call dispatch: lib/mcp/server/transports/streamable_http_transport.rb:731 -> lib/mcp/server.rb:617 call_tool -> app tool.call (server.rb:844-864).

trace.note: handle_request routes POST to handle_post
handle_post checks Accept and Content-Type only; no Origin/Host check
initialize creates session without any auth
handle_regular_request with session ID
dispatch to server.handle_json
call_tool invokes app tool

finding.guards_checked: Accept header check (streamable_http_transport.rb:528-539): not a cross-origin control. Content-Type must be application/json (:547-557): blocks classic form/text-plain CSRF but not DNS rebinding. Session ID required (:719-720): obtained from open initialize. MCP-Protocol-Version header (:585-595): attacker sets it. No Origin/Host control exists.

finding.claim: OAuth client fetches URLs supplied by an untrusted MCP server (WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata, PRM authorization_servers, AS metadata endpoints) with no host restriction. Only an https check, or any http URL on loopback, is applied, so a malicious server can make the client GET internal https hosts or loopback services. Blind SSRF / port-probe oracle; low to medium.
finding.source: Untrusted MCP server's 401 WWW-Authenticate header (resource_metadata parameter) and PRM body (authorization_servers) when the client is configured with oauth:.
finding.sink: Outbound HTTP GET: lib/mcp/client/oauth/flow.rb:764-766 http_get via fetch_metadata_json (flow.rb:333-367); token/registration POSTs at flow.rb:674-737 and :442-443.

trace.note: parse_www_authenticate_from_error reads WWW-Authenticate from server 401
run_oauth_flow! passes resource_metadata into flow
run! calls ensure_secure_url! on resource_metadata_url
secure_url? accepts any https host, or http when loopback_host? (discovery.rb:189)
fetch_protected_resource_metadata issues GET
authorization_servers[0] only checked with ensure_secure_url!
AS metadata GET to attacker-chosen issuer
http_get -> Faraday GET with no host or IP allowlist

finding.guards_checked: ensure_secure_url! on resource_metadata (flow.rb:37-38, 380-385); ensure_secure_url! on authorization_servers entry (flow.rb:237); ensure_secure_endpoints! on AS metadata (flow.rb:266, 387-392); issuer match on modern path (flow.rb:402-412); resource_covers? audience check (flow.rb:513-525), which runs only after the fetch; Faraday does not follow redirects by default. No destination-host or private-address restriction exists; loopback http is explicitly allowed (discovery.rb:189).

finding.claim: Session validation is skipped for notifications. A notification with an unknown or expired Mcp-Session-Id is accepted and dispatched to server-level handlers with no session, while requests with an unknown session get 404. Impact is limited to app-registered sessionless notification handlers; SDK built-in notification handlers are no-ops without a session.
finding.source: Any client POSTing a JSON-RPC notification with an arbitrary Mcp-Session-Id header value.
finding.sink: Server-level notification dispatch: streamable_http_transport.rb:412-414 -> dispatch_notification (:608-622) -> @server.handle_json (:619, :795) -> server.rb:447-449 handler lookup, with session = nil.

trace.note: initialize check; non-initialize path only validates protocol version
only the missing-session check; no validity check
notification branch
session lookup returns nil for unknown or expired ID; no expiry check
dispatch with server_session = nil
notifications/cancelled no-ops when session is nil (server.rb:519-521)

finding.guards_checked: Missing-session check (streamable_http_transport.rb:393). Protocol-version header check (:395-397). Request path validate_and_touch_session (:719-720) is not applied to notifications. Notification handlers without a session are no-ops for SDK built-ins (server.rb:519-528).

finding.claim: Instrumentation state is stored on the shared Server instance, not per request. Concurrent requests overwrite each other's @instrumentation_data, so the instrumentation callback can receive another request's data, including tool_arguments. Low severity: telemetry mis-attribution and cross-request data mixing.
finding.source: Concurrent requests on the multi-threaded StreamableHTTPTransport; tool_arguments stored at server.rb:628.
finding.sink: Instrumentation callback: lib/mcp/instrumentation.rb:39 configuration.instrumentation_callback.call(@instrumentation_data); also add_instrumentation_data writes at :43-45.

trace.note: instrument_call resets @instrumentation_data = {} on the shared Server object
request body runs; other threads may reset the hash during this time
add_instrumentation_data(tool_arguments: arguments) writes into the shared hash
ensure block passes whatever hash is current to the callback

finding.guards_checked: None. The race is not guarded by a mutex or per-request storage. Reporting-side guard: exception_already_reported check (instrumentation.rb:15-16) does not cover this.
